decision: Architecture acceptable; root must explicitly adopt or decline the two minor clarifications before freezing the corpus. Implementation dispatch remains subject to the existing ownership/provisioning/release coordination preconditions.

findings.title: Freeze the canonical encoder and explicit digest payloads
findings.problem: Sorted keys and no whitespace do not uniquely specify UTF-8 JSON bytes. Go default encoding escapes HTML and U+2028/U+2029; JavaScript JSON.stringify does not make the same choices. Round-trippable FLOAT64 text is also not unique. ReadPlan contains its own digest, and the contract needs an explicit hash projection rather than hashing the self-containing object. The mandated corpus can close this before implementation; this is not a reason to add a core interface.
findings.amendment: Use RFC 8785 JCS for the adapter-owned canonical JSON payload: valid Unicode scalar strings, no Unicode normalization, UTF-16 code-unit property order, its exact string escaping and UTF-8 bytes. Reject unpaired surrogates. All numeric JSON tokens in these payloads are bounded exact safe integers; warehouse integer/decimal values remain canonical strings. Finite FLOAT64 strings use ECMAScript NumberToString (including its exponent thresholds), normalizing negative zero to "0", with the same formatter semantics in Go. Define named hash payloads: ReadPlan hashes exactly version/sourceDigest/projection/where/order/limit/parameters/sql, omitting only its top-level digest; SourceProfile hashes all declared fields; the observation binding hashes only exact table identity/location/native type/config/schema; approval hashes the declared binding fields (effective plan, observation and policy digests, execution principal including generation, project/location, cap/budget/bounds and estimate), excluding its own digest and the explicitly unbound times/nonce. Do not recursively delete properties named digest from arbitrary values. Publish these exact payload schemas and canonical bytes in the frozen corpus.
conformance: Go and JS produce identical bytes and SHA-256 for strings containing quotes, backslashes, control characters, <>&, U+2028/U+2029 and supplementary characters.
Non-BMP property ordering follows UTF-16; lone surrogate is rejected; composed/decomposed Unicode strings remain distinct.
FLOAT64 cases -0, 1e-7, 1e-6, 1e20 and 1e21 have identical strings and digests.
Changing a top-level digest field alone leaves its named underlying digest calculation unchanged; changing a bound parameter or cap changes approval; excluded observation/preview timestamps do not.

findings.title: Make the run deadline persistent across Resume
findings.problem: The contract persists counters and bounds but does not name when wallMs starts or whether paused/process-exit time counts. A new Resume context could unintentionally restart 120 seconds. Status and cancel need their stated recovery role without giving paging a fresh execution budget.
findings.amendment: At the start of run reauthorization/pre-submit preparation, persist runStartedAt and executionDeadline = runStartedAt + wallMs in the trusted ledger. The execution deadline is absolute; stopped/offline time counts. All run metadata/dry-run/recheck/submission/poll/page operations, including Resume, use the earlier of caller deadline, per-HTTP timeout and this original executionDeadline. Resume never changes the deadline or resets row/page/byte counters. Once expired, result reads return local_stopped with a deadline reason and the existing receipt without network dispatch. Explicit status/cancel may use a fresh control context of at most 15 seconds after that deadline, but cannot read rows, rerun a query, renew approval, reset cumulative byte counters or release a reservation without authoritative terminal billing evidence. They retain bounded responses and existing cumulative byte accounting; if those bytes are exhausted, return the bound error and retain the reservation. Preview has its own bounded operation and the existing five-minute approval TTL; time awaiting user approval is not charged to a run that has not started.
conformance: With a fake clock, stop at 119 seconds and resume at 121: zero page/POST requests, original deadline and counters unchanged, partial receipt retained.
Resume before deadline permits only the remaining time; GET retries and backoff consume that time.
Status/cancel after execution deadline use fresh <=15-second control contexts; they never reset execution limits or submit queries.
Exhausted cumulative bytes reject further control responses safely and retain unresolved reservation; completed status with valid billing reconciles only the existing job.
